problems.quote: The term was coined by Augustin Pyramus de Candolle , who is called the Father of Taxonomy.
problems.problem: Wrong attribution: 'Father of Taxonomy' is Carl Linnaeus, not Augustin Pyramus de Candolle. De Candolle coined the term 'taxonomy'.
problems.correction: The term was coined by Augustin Pyramus de Candolle; Carl Linnaeus is called the Father of Taxonomy.
problems.verifierReason: De Candolle coined 'taxonomy'; Linnaeus is Father of Taxonomy. Original conflates them.

problems.quote: Smallest living cells (0.1-0.3 m).
problems.problem: Wrong unit: size given in meters (m) instead of micrometers (µm). Mycoplasma are 0.1-0.3 µm.
problems.correction: Smallest living cells (0.1-0.3 µm).
problems.verifierReason: 0.1-0.3 m is 10-30 cm; mycoplasmas are 0.1-0.3 µm. Unit error is clear.

problems.quote: When V C, a mixed ESS exists with proportion p = V/C of Hawks
problems.problem: Missing inequality sign; the condition for a mixed ESS in the Hawk-Dove game is V < C, not 'V C'.
problems.correction: When V < C, a mixed ESS exists with proportion p = V/C of Hawks
problems.verifierReason: Original quote missing inequality operator; mixed ESS requires V < C for 0 < p < 1. Correction is standard textbook result.

problems.quote: Additional features include a ventral heart and a closed circulatory system.
problems.problem: These are vertebrate features, not universal chordate features; many chordates (e.g., tunicates, lancelets) lack a true heart and/or have open circulation.
problems.correction: Additional vertebrate features include a ventral heart and a closed circulatory system.
problems.verifierReason: Original incorrectly assigns ventral heart & closed circulation to all chordates; lancelets lack heart, tunicates have open circulation. Correction accurately restricts to vertebrates.

problems.quote: Cyclostomata (jawless, ectoparasitic — lamprey, hagfish).
problems.problem: Hagfish are scavengers, not ectoparasites; only lampreys are ectoparasitic.
problems.correction: Cyclostomata (jawless; lampreys ectoparasitic, hagfish scavengers — lamprey, hagfish).
problems.verifierReason: Hagfish are scavengers/predators, not ectoparasites; only lampreys are ectoparasitic. Original overgeneralizes Cyclostomata. Correction accurately distinguishes feeding modes.

problems.quote: eurphaline
problems.problem: Misspelling of the term for organisms tolerating a wide salinity range; correct term is 'euryhaline'.
problems.correction: euryhaline
problems.verifierReason: Original 'eurphaline' is misspelled; correct term is 'euryhaline' (Greek eurys + halinos).

problems.quote: Paramoecium
problems.problem: Misspelling of the genus name used in Gause's experiments; correct genus is 'Paramecium'.
problems.correction: Paramecium
problems.verifierReason: Original 'Paramoecium' is outdated/misspelled; accepted genus is 'Paramecium'.

problems.quote: dN/dt = rN(K N)/K
problems.problem: The logistic growth equation is missing a minus sign; it should be dN/dt = rN(K - N)/K or dN/dt = rN(1 - N/K).
problems.correction: dN/dt = rN(K - N)/K
problems.verifierReason: Original lacks minus sign; logistic growth requires (K-N). Correction is standard form.

problems.quote: (K N)/K
problems.problem: The expression (K N)/K is missing a minus sign; it should be (K - N)/K.
problems.correction: (K - N)/K
problems.verifierReason: Expression (K N)/K simplifies to N; logistic term requires (K-N)/K. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: release acetylcholine onto muscarinic receptors
problems.problem: Parasympathetic preganglionic fibers release acetylcholine onto nicotinic receptors on postganglionic neurons; muscarinic receptors are on effector organs and are activated by postganglionic fibers.
problems.correction: release acetylcholine onto nicotinic receptors
problems.verifierReason: Original statement misidentifies receptor type; correction to nicotinic receptors matches autonomic physiology.

problems.quote: suppressed serum ADH
problems.problem: In SIADH, serum ADH is inappropriately normal or elevated (non-suppressed) relative to low plasma osmolality; it is not suppressed.
problems.correction: non-suppressed ADH
problems.verifierReason: In SIADH ADH is inappropriately normal or elevated, not suppressed; correction is accurate.

problems.quote: 14th Report (1958) on abolition of jury trials
problems.problem: The 14th Law Commission Report (1958) did not deal with abolition of jury trials; the 41st Report (1969) recommended abolition of jury trials.
problems.correction: 41st Report (1969) on abolition of jury trials
problems.verifierReason: 14th Report (1958) was on judicial administration; 41st Report (1969) recommended abolishing jury trials.

problems.quote: the Governor should be consulted before appointment
problems.problem: The Sarkaria Commission recommended that the Chief Minister should be consulted before appointment of the Governor, not that the Governor should be consulted.
problems.correction: the Chief Minister should be consulted before appointment of the Governor
problems.verifierReason: Sarkaria Commission (1988) recommended CM be consulted before Governor's appointment, not Governor.

problems.quote: The value of z is typically 0.1 0.2 for mainland (continuous habitat) surveys and 0.6 0.7 for islands or isolated habitats
problems.problem: The typical z value for islands is 0.2–0.3, not 0.6–0.7.
problems.correction: The value of z is typically 0.1–0.2 for mainland surveys and 0.2–0.3 for islands or isolated habitats.
problems.verifierReason: Standard ecology texts (MacArthur & Wilson; Rosenzweig) give island z ~0.25–0.35, not 0.6–0.7. Correction matches consensus.

problems.quote: PM 2.5 fine particles 2.5 m in diameter
problems.problem: PM2.5 particle size given in meters instead of micrometers
problems.correction: PM 2.5 fine particles 2.5 µm in diameter
problems.verifierReason: PM2.5 definition is 2.5 micrometers, not meters. Correction is accurate.

problems.quote: PM 10 coarse particles 10 m
problems.problem: PM10 particle size given in meters instead of micrometers
problems.correction: PM 10 coarse particles 10 µm
problems.verifierReason: PM10 definition is 10 micrometers, not meters. Correction is accurate.

problems.quote: Drinking water BOD 5 mg/L
problems.problem: Drinking water BOD is not 5 mg/L; it should be much lower (<1 mg/L)
problems.correction: Drinking water BOD <1 mg/L
problems.verifierReason: Drinking water BOD limit is <1 mg/L per BIS 10500; 5 mg/L is wastewater standard.

problems.quote: altered DNA methylation at multiple CpG islands
problems.problem: The vinclozolin study (Anway et al., 2005) identified differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that were largely not in CpG islands; they were in CpG-poor regions.
problems.correction: altered DNA methylation at multiple differentially methylated regions
problems.verifierReason: Anway et al. 2005 explicitly states DMRs were largely not in CpG islands but in CpG-poor regions.

problems.quote: about 18 C instead of the actual +15 C
problems.problem: The temperature without the natural greenhouse effect is approximately -18°C, not +18°C.
problems.correction: about -18°C instead of the actual +15°C
problems.verifierReason: Original misses minus sign; effective temperature without greenhouse effect is -18°C, not +18°C. Correction adds minus sign accurately.

problems.quote: net: O 3 + O 2O 2
problems.problem: The net reaction for the catalytic ozone destruction cycle is O3 + O → 2O2; the given equation is missing an oxygen atom and the reaction arrow.
problems.correction: net: O3 + O → 2O2
problems.verifierReason: Original lacks reaction arrow and clear stoichiometry; corrected net reaction O3 + O → 2O2 is standard for catalytic ozone destruction cycles.

problems.quote: the 2001 Census identified 52 million slum dwellers
problems.problem: The 2001 Census of India reported the slum population as approximately 42.6 million, not 52 million.
problems.correction: the 2001 Census identified 42.6 million slum dwellers
problems.verifierReason: 2001 Census reported 42.6M slum dwellers, not 52M.

problems.quote: Dharavi’s recycling economy generating an estimated annual turnover of ₹1 billion
problems.problem: The widely cited estimate for Dharavi's annual turnover is around $1 billion (approx. ₹7,000 crore), not ₹1 billion (₹100 crore).
problems.correction: Dharavi’s recycling economy generating an estimated annual turnover of $1 billion (approx. ₹7,000 crore)
problems.verifierReason: Dharavi turnover widely cited as $1B (~₹7,000 cr), not ₹1B.

problems.quote: Hyderabad (Telangana) — directly elected Mayor
problems.problem: The Mayor of Hyderabad is not directly elected; the Mayor is indirectly elected by the corporators.
problems.correction: Hyderabad (Telangana) — indirectly elected Mayor
problems.verifierReason: Hyderabad Mayor is indirectly elected by corporators per GHMC Act.

problems.quote: The 74th Amendment recommended the Nagarpalika Bill 1992 which provided for a directly elected Mayor with a fixed 5-year term
problems.problem: The 74th Amendment (Nagarpalika Bill 1992) did not mandate a directly elected Mayor; it left the manner of election to state legislatures.
problems.correction: The 74th Amendment left the manner of election of the Mayor to state legislatures
problems.verifierReason: 74th Amendment leaves mayoral election mode to states; does not mandate direct election.

problems.quote: State and central grants are untied but come with conditions.
problems.problem: Grants are often tied (conditional); untied grants by definition have no conditions. The statement is contradictory and factually incorrect.
problems.correction: State and central grants are often tied and come with conditions.
problems.verifierReason: Untied grants have no conditions; many grants are tied (conditional).

problems.quote: The Supreme Court in A.K. Roy v. Union of India (1981) held that residuary power includes power to legislate on matters like prevention of detention, though other provisions of the Constitution may al
problems.problem: Preventive detention is explicitly allocated in the Union List (Entry 9) and Concurrent List (Entry 3); the case did not treat it as a residuary subject.
problems.correction: The Supreme Court in A.K. Roy v. Union of India (1981) upheld Parliament's power to legislate on preventive detention under the Union List.
problems.verifierReason: A.K. Roy upheld preventive detention law under Union List, not residuary power.

problems.quote: appear explicitly in the General Studies syllabus under economy, statistics and technology sections
problems.problem: The UPSC General Studies syllabus does not have a separate "statistics" section; statistical topics are subsumed under economy and other areas.
problems.correction: appear explicitly in the General Studies syllabus under economy and technology sections
problems.verifierReason: UPSC GS syllabus lacks a separate statistics section; removal is correct.

problems.quote: creating a “demographic dividend” for sending countries (remittances)
problems.problem: The term "demographic dividend" refers to the economic growth potential arising from a favorable age structure (rising working-age share), not to remittance inflows. Remittances are a separate benefit of migration.
problems.correction: creating economic benefits for sending countries through remittances
problems.verifierReason: Original misuses 'demographic dividend' (age-structure growth potential) to mean remittances. Correction accurately describes remittances as economic benefits.

problems.quote: The compensation period was extended beyond 2022 through borrowing arrangements.
problems.problem: The GST compensation period ended in June 2022; it was not extended. Borrowings were made to cover the shortfall during the compensation period.
problems.correction: The compensation period ended in 2022; borrowings were used to cover the shortfall during the period.
problems.verifierReason: GST compensation period ended June 2022; borrowings covered shortfall during period, did not extend it.

problems.quote: As of 2025, the compensation mechanism has been restructured with continued support to states facing revenue shortfalls.
problems.problem: There is no restructured compensation mechanism; the compensation period ended. The cess continues only to repay borrowings.
problems.correction: As of 2025, the compensation cess continues to be levied to repay borrowings taken during the compensation period.
problems.verifierReason: No restructured mechanism; compensation ended 2022, cess continues only for loan repayment.

problems.quote: Ayushman Bharat
problems.problem: Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) is a Central Sector Scheme, not a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
problems.correction: Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) is a Central Sector Scheme.
problems.verifierReason: PM-JAY is Central Sector Scheme; Ayushman Bharat includes HWCs (CSS) but PM-JAY is core.

problems.quote: PM Awas Yojana (Central component)
problems.problem: PM Awas Yojana is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme; there is no separate central component that is a Central Sector Scheme.
problems.correction: PM Awas Yojana is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
problems.verifierReason: PMAY-Urban and Gramin are Centrally Sponsored Schemes; no separate Central Sector component.

problems.quote: n ( θ̂ − θ ) converges to an exponential law
problems.problem: For the uniform distribution on [0, θ], the MLE is θ̂ = max X_i ≤ θ, so θ̂ − θ ≤ 0. The correct limiting distribution is that n(θ − θ̂) converges to an exponential law (or n(θ̂ − θ) converges to the negative of an exponential).
problems.correction: n ( θ − θ̂ ) converges to an exponential law
problems.verifierReason: For Uniform(0,θ) MLE, n(θ̂-θ) ≤ 0; limit is negative exponential. Correction n(θ-θ̂) → Exp is accurate.

problems.quote: Unlike the USA and Australia (where there is dual citizenship — of the Union and of the individual State)
problems.problem: Australia does not have dual citizenship; it has a single national citizenship.
problems.correction: Unlike the USA (where there is dual citizenship — of the Union and of the individual State)
problems.verifierReason: Australia has only single national citizenship; no state citizenship exists.
